cards.front: What is perimeter?
cards.back: The distance all the way around the outside of a shape.
cards.say: What is perimeter? The distance all the way around the outside of a shape.

cards.front: What is area?
cards.back: The amount of flat space inside a shape, measured in square units such as cm².
cards.say: What is area? The amount of flat space inside a shape, measured in square units such as square centimetres.

cards.front: What is volume?
cards.back: The amount of space inside a 3D shape, measured in cubic units such as cm³.
cards.say: What is volume? The amount of space inside a three D shape, measured in cubic units such as cubic centimetres.

cards.front: Area of a rectangle
cards.back: length × width. Example: 8 cm by 5 cm has area 40 cm².
cards.say: Area of a rectangle is length times width. Example: eight centimetres by five centimetres has area forty square centimetres.

cards.front: Perimeter of a rectangle
cards.back: 2 × (length + width), or add all four sides. Example: 8 cm by 5 cm has perimeter 26 cm.
cards.say: Perimeter of a rectangle. Two times, length plus width, or add all four sides. Example: eight centimetres by five centimetres has perimeter twenty six centimetres.

cards.front: Area of a square with side 7 cm
cards.say: Area of a square with side seven centimetres. Forty nine square centimetres, because seven times seven equals forty nine.

cards.front: Perimeter of a square with side 7 cm
cards.say: Perimeter of a square with side seven centimetres. Twenty eight centimetres, because four times seven equals twenty eight.

cards.front: Perimeter of a regular hexagon with side 5 cm
cards.back: 30 cm. A hexagon has 6 equal sides and 6 × 5 = 30.
cards.say: Perimeter of a regular hexagon with side five centimetres. Thirty centimetres. A hexagon has six equal sides, and six times five equals thirty.

cards.front: A rectangle has area 36 cm² and width 4 cm. Find its length.
cards.say: A rectangle has area thirty six square centimetres and width four centimetres. Find its length. Nine centimetres, because thirty six divided by four equals nine.

cards.front: A rectangle has perimeter 20 cm and length 6 cm. Find its width.
cards.back: 4 cm. Two lengths use 12 cm, leaving 8 cm for two widths, so each width is 4 cm.
cards.say: A rectangle has perimeter twenty centimetres and length six centimetres. Find its width. Four centimetres. Two lengths use twelve, leaving eight for two widths, so each width is four.

cards.front: An L-shape is a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle with a 2 cm by 2 cm square cut from a corner. Find its area.
cards.say: An L shape is a six by four centimetre rectangle with a two by two centimetre square cut from a corner. Find its area. Twenty square centimetres, because twenty four minus four is twenty.

cards.front: Which unit measures area: cm, cm² or cm³?
cards.say: Which unit measures area: centimetres, square centimetres or cubic centimetres? Square centimetres. Square units measure area.

cards.front: Which unit measures volume: cm, cm² or cm³?
cards.say: Which unit measures volume: centimetres, square centimetres or cubic centimetres? Cubic centimetres. Cubic units measure volume.

cards.front: Volume of a cuboid
cards.back: length × width × height. Example: 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm has volume 24 cm³.
cards.say: Volume of a cuboid is length times width times height. Example: four centimetres by three centimetres by two centimetres has volume twenty four cubic centimetres.

cards.front: Volume of a cube with side 3 cm
cards.say: Volume of a cube with side three centimetres. Twenty seven cubic centimetres, because three times three times three equals twenty seven.

cards.front: Volume of a cuboid 10 cm by 5 cm by 2 cm
cards.say: Volume of a cuboid ten centimetres by five centimetres by two centimetres. One hundred cubic centimetres, because ten times five equals fifty, and fifty times two equals one hundred.

cards.front: What is a cubic centimetre?
cards.back: The volume of a cube with edges 1 cm long. We write it 1 cm³.
cards.say: What is a cubic centimetre? The volume of a cube with edges one centimetre long.

cards.front: How many mL are in 1 cm³?
cards.back: 1 mL. One cubic centimetre holds one millilitre.
cards.say: How many millilitres are in one cubic centimetre? One millilitre.

cards.front: How many cm³ make 1 litre?
cards.say: How many cubic centimetres make one litre? One thousand cubic centimetres.

cards.front: A box holds 100 cm³. How many mL of water fill it?
cards.say: A box holds one hundred cubic centimetres. How many millilitres of water fill it? One hundred millilitres, because one cubic centimetre holds one millilitre.

cards.front: How many cm² in 1 m²?
cards.say: How many square centimetres in one square metre? Ten thousand. One hundred times one hundred equals ten thousand.

cards.front: A room is 3 m by 2 m. What is its area?
cards.say: A room is three metres by two metres. What is its area? Six square metres. Three times two equals six.

cards.front: If you double the side of a square, does its perimeter double too?
cards.back: Yes. Perimeter is 4 × side, so doubling the side doubles the perimeter. (The area becomes 4 times as big.)
cards.say: If you double the side of a square, does its perimeter double too? Yes. Perimeter is four times the side, so doubling the side doubles the perimeter. The area becomes four times as big.
